hints.title: Multi-Source Distance Diffusion Obstacle
hints.text: Computing distance to the nearest 0 by searching outward from every 1 cell repeats paths across identical subgrids. How can multi-source propagation starting from all 0 cells determine minimum distances simultaneously?

hints.title: Wavefront Layer Monotonicity Invariant
hints.text: All 0 cells have distance 0. Expanding simultaneously layer by layer guarantees that any cell reached at wave step d receives its minimal distance d.

hints.title: Multi-Source Wave Queue Procedure
hints.text: Initialize a distance matrix dist with -1. Enqueue all coordinates with value 0, setting dist[r][c] = 0. While the queue has elements, pop (r, c). For each 4-directional neighbor (nr, nc): if within bounds and dist[nr][nc] == -1, set dist[nr][nc] = dist[r][c] + 1 and enqueue (nr, nc).

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Every cell is enqueued and processed exactly once in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Searching outward from every 1 cell takes O((M * N)^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Distance matrix and queue occupy O(M * N) auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using all 0 cells as the multi-source origin wave.
